# Disagreement Log — Gospel of Thomas, Saying 29

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Saying:** GTH 029
**Total Disagreements:** 3

---

## Disagreement 1 — "marvel" vs. "amazing"

**Verse:** vv.1-2
**EMET/LOGOS:** "marvel" / "marvel of marvels"
**PNEUMA:** "amazing" / "amazing beyond amazing"
**Issue:** *Špēre* = wonder, marvel. "Marvel" is the noun; "amazing" is an adjective. The noun form is more appropriate. "Marvel of marvels" is an established superlative form (cf. "holy of holies").
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Marvel" / "marvel of marvels" retained.

---

## Disagreement 2 — "made its home" vs. "come to live in"

**Verse:** v.3
**EMET/LOGOS:** "made its home"
**PNEUMA:** "come to live in"
**Issue:** *Mauet* = to dwell, make one's abode. "Made its home" preserves the established dwelling. "Come to live in" implies a recent arrival.
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Made its home" retained.

---

## Disagreement 3 — connection to "poverty" in Saying 3

**All agents:** Note the word *kēke* (poverty) recurs
**Issue:** Should the SOPHIA note explicitly connect Saying 29's "poverty" to Saying 3's "poverty"?
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** Yes — the connection is noted in consensus notes as a productive tension between the two uses of the same word.
